title: AI Could Make Governments Slower
gist: Sami Mahroum argues AI adoption in government may reduce rather than raise throughput, because finite human attention becomes the bottleneck wherever oversight is required — evidenced by US federal courts, where pro-se filings jumped from an 11% average in 2005-22 to 16.8% in 2025 and machine-written civil complaints went from 1% in 2023 to 18% today.

insights.claim: Making machines more capable does not automatically raise institutional throughput, because human attention is finite and becomes a new bottleneck wherever oversight is necessary.
insights.speaker: Sami Mahroum
insights.so_what: A counterweight to blanket AI-productivity assumptions: model the human review step as the capacity constraint when sizing AI-driven efficiency gains in regulated or supervised workflows.
insights.quote: because human attention is finite, making machines more capable could simply create new bottlenecks wherever oversight is necessary

insights.claim: The share of US federal lawsuits filed without a lawyer rose from an 11% average over 2005-22 to 16.8% in 2025, a surge researchers link to the advent of AI.
insights.speaker: Sami Mahroum
insights.so_what: Hard evidence that generative AI is expanding volume in legal systems — a demand tailwind for legal-tech triage and a cost headwind for court and compliance budgets.

insights.so_what: Quantifies how fast AI-generated text is saturating a formal institutional channel; expect detection, verification and review services to become a required cost line.

insights.claim: Institutions have been struggling to keep up with AI-generated writing since ChatGPT's 2022 release, with courts the clearest pressure point.
insights.speaker: Sami Mahroum
insights.so_what: Courts are the leading indicator for AI-driven volume shocks in other document-heavy institutions such as regulators, insurers and benefits agencies.

insights.claim: Governments are turning to AI to process vast amounts of information and make public services more efficient, so the efficiency case is being adopted before the oversight bottleneck is priced in.
insights.speaker: Sami Mahroum
insights.so_what: Public-sector AI budgets are expanding now; vendors selling throughput may face disappointment cycles when oversight capacity fails to scale.
